instruction: Camera Silhouette Optimization. `init_file/scene.blend` contains: - A single asymmetric mesh object named `Target` centered at the world origin. Its bounding box is roughly 3.0 (X) x 0.5 (Y) x 2.0 (Z), with a small bump that breaks symmetry. The Y-axis is the shortest, so viewing the object along +/-Y reveals the widest cross-section (approximately X*Z = 6 square units in world space). - A `Camera` named `Camera`, configured ORTHOGRAPHIC with `cam.data.ortho_scale = 5.0` and placed at distance 5.0 from the origin at some arbitrary initial angle (e.g. Azimuth 30 deg, elevation 15 deg). It is NOT currently at the optimum orientation. - A pure-white World background. - Render engine: Cycles CPU, 4 samples, denoising off. - Resolution 256x256, RGBA PNG, `scene.render.film_transparent = True` so the render's alpha is 1.0 where the object is visible and 0.0 elsewhere. - View Transform: Standard. Task: find the camera orientation (azimuth, elevation) on a sphere of radius 5 around the origin that MAXIMIZES the silhouette area of `Target` in the rendered image (the silhouette area is the count of pixels whose alpha > 0.5). Then set the camera to that optimum orientation, render once to `ground_truth/output/optimal.png` at 256x256, and save the.blend to `ground_truth/answer.blend`. ## Required steps 1. Open `init_file/scene.blend`. 2. Brute-force search: iterate azimuth over [0, 360) in steps of 10 degrees and elevation over [-80, +80] in steps of 10 degrees (you may refine on a finer grid afterward). For each (az, el): - Position the Camera at `(r*cos(el)*cos(az), r*cos(el)*sin(az), r*sin(el))` with `r = 5.0`. - Orient it to look at the origin. The standard recipe is: `from mathutils import Vector` `direction = Vector((0,0,0)) - cam.location` `cam.rotation_mode = 'QUATERNION'` `cam.rotation_quaternion = direction.to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y')` - Render to a temp file, load the PNG with `bpy.data.images.load(...)`, count pixels whose alpha > 0.5, then remove the image datablock. 3. Keep the (az*, el*) that gives the largest silhouette area. 4. Set the camera to (az*, el*), render the final image to `ground_truth/output/optimal.png` (256x256, RGBA), and save the.blend as `ground_truth/answer.blend`. ## Hints / gotchas - Camera is orthographic so the silhouette area does NOT depend on distance. - `scene.render.film_transparent = True` is already set; preserve it. - Keep the Cycles sample count low (4) for speed; 36*17 = 612 renders at 256x256 is still tractable in a few minutes. - Count alpha-positive pixels using Blender's own image API so you do not need numpy: `img.pixels[3::4]` gives alpha values. 1. `ground_truth/answer.blend` exists and opens in Blender. 2. Scene contains a `Target` object (mesh) centered near the origin. 3. Scene contains a `Camera` object (type CAMERA) as the active `scene.camera`. 4. `ground_truth/output/optimal.png` exists. 5. The rendered PNG is exactly 256x256. 6. The submitted render has silhouette area (alpha > 0.5 pixel count) >= 1000 pixels (object is visible, not edge-on). 7. The submitted camera orientation yields a silhouette area within 2% of the true analytical optimum: the eval renders ONE image at the camera's current orientation and ONE image at the known optimum (camera on the +Y axis at distance 5, looking at origin, orthographic) and requires `submitted_area >= 0.98 * optimum_area`.
source: Vázquez, Feixas, Sbert, Heidrich 2001 — "Viewpoint Selection using Viewpoint Entropy", VMV
